title: Smart pointers: Box, Rc, Arc, and Mutex

spans.text: LESSON PURPOSE

Goal: apply “Smart pointers: Box, Rc, Arc, and Mutex” to a real program or device. The key principle is: Arc shares ownership across threads; Mutex serializes mutable access to the critical section. In a project, follow this guidance: Arc<Mutex<T>> is not always the best design; consider message passing before shared mutable state.

CORE EXPLANATION

Box<T> stores a value on the heap and enables recursive structures with a fixed-size pointer. Rc<T> provides reference-counted sharing within one thread; Arc<T> uses an atomic count for cross-thread sharing, but neither makes shared mutation automatically safe. Mutable shared state needs synchronization such as Mutex/RwLock and careful lock scopes.
IMPORTANT LINE BREAKDOWN

If omitted or changed: Slow I/O while holding a lock increases deadlock and latency risk; handle poisoning too.
